text:
Arjun: Heads-up — ran a 1k-conversation smoke suite on the INT8 weight-only AWQ build after the recent packing heuristic change. Seeing a consistent 6–11% p95 increase on short-chat workloads (seq_len <= 128).
Sara: oh no. did the KV cache hit pattern change?
Arjun: KV hit ratio is the same. The regression surfaces in GPU activity during kv pack/unpack phases. Kernel-switch trace shows more fallback to the generic matmul for certain group sizes.
Lee: can you paste the pprof flame or nvprof snippet?
Arjun: pasted below — this is a condensed nvprof sample (time in ms over 100 requests):

```
NVPROF: Kernel times (sampled)
awq_pack_kernel           14.2 ms  (was 9.1 ms pre-change)
kv_serialize             3.5 ms
matmul_int8_generic      21.7 ms  (was 16.2 ms pre-change)
kv_unpack               2.8 ms
other                    4.1 ms
TOTAL (on-GPU)          46.3 ms (was ~37.4 ms)
```

Arjun: the pattern is: pack kernel heavier due to extra alignment step we added to support uneven group sizes, and more matmul_generic because group-size-aware kernels aren't being selected when packing splits vectors across warp boundaries.
Marta: which group sizes are hitting it?
Arjun: mostly g=32->g=16 transitions for some layers in 13B models when layer dim mod group !=0. Quick microbench below (throughput tokens/s):

```
Group | AWQ throughput | GPTQ throughput
16    | 1020 tok/s      | 980 tok/s
24    | 1185 tok/s      | 1150 tok/s
32    | 1210 tok/s      | 1198 tok/s
40    | 1165 tok/s      | 1140 tok/s
```

Arjun: The new packing alignment nudges some layers from 32->24 behavior which increases kernel fragmentation.
Sara: hmm. Could also be branch mispredicts during calibration lookup — we added that tiny clamp table right?
Lee: yes we did the clamp lookup for scale/table fallback. Branch density up by ~15% in the pack kernel according to shader stats. That explains the tick up.
Marta: Two ideas: 1) make alignment optional per-layer based on layer dim % group and estimated fragmentation cost; 2) try a vectored memcpy to avoid conditional branches in the clamp lookup.
Arjun: I ran a quick experiment toggling alignment off for layers where (dim % group == 0). Result: p95 drops back to baseline for short chats, overall throughput +4%.
perf-bot: [perf/regress] ALERT: CI run 2026-03-18-07:23 detected 8.4% p95 regression on int8-awq-ops vs baseline. Link: https://perf.redwood/ci/1977654321
Sara: good catch by perf-bot — CI also shows matching allocation spikes in pinned host memory during packing. So packing change increased host<->device pinned alloc churn.
Lee: pinned alloc churn indicates our temp buffer allocation path isn't reusing the aligned scratch buffer. Packing alignment changes increased buffer size variance causing new allocs.
Marta: If we pre-reserve the max-aligned scratch buffer per model and reuse it, pinned churn should go away. Also consider amortizing pack cost across KV reuse by caching packed representations for short-lived keys.
Arjun: Agreed. For immediate mitigation I've: 1) toggled alignment off for clean divisors, 2) added a simple scratch-buffer pool for pinned memory. Nightly runs show regression gone, p95 within 1% of baseline.
Sara: can we add a unit test that emulates worst-case dim%group skew and asserts no >5% p95 regression on short seq tests?
Lee: yea I'll add a microbenchmark that runs the pack kernel across a histogram of dims and group sizes and checks kernel selection counts.
Marta: longer term we should evaluate adaptive group-size selection: pick per-layer group so kernel path remains contiguous and avoid pack-time fragmenting. Also consider making the clamp-luookup branch-free (table lookup + masked islands).
Arjun: next experiments planned: (A) pool + alignment heuristics (already landed in a branch), (B) branchless clamp, (C) cached packed KV for hot keys. I'll post numbers tomorrow.
Sara: small doc request — add a quick note in the eng-runtime runbook about 'packed scratch pool' and the heuristic toggle so oncall knows the rollback knob.
Marta: also tag ops and perf for a regression watch for the next week.
Arjun: thanks — will do. Posting the short reproducer here for anyone who wants to run:

```
# reproducer (py):
for group in [16,24,32,40]:
    run_microbench(model='13B-awq', seq_len=64, group=group, repeat=200)
    collect_kernel_trace('nvprof')
```

Arjun: TL;DR: packing alignment change + un-reused pinned buffers caused extra matmul fallbacks and host alloc churn -> p95 regression. Mitigations: per-layer alignment gating + pinned scratch pool.
Lee: awesome triage. If perf-bot keeps alerting after fixes, we'll bisect to the exact commit.
perf-bot: [perf/notify] NOTE: Mitigations branch 1977654321-fix-pack-pool pushed. Running canary suite.
